title: FDR's 1937 Desert Game Range guarded by anti-aircraft guns 'to protect bighorn sheep'
place_text: Desert Game Range / Sheep Peak, Nevada

tellings.quote: Now, the Desert Game Range was set up in the time of Franklin D. Roosevelt.

plain: The Desert Game Range in Nevada, around Sheep Peak, was set up under President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1937, and was guarded by anti-aircraft guns, supposedly to protect the bighorn sheep. Charles Hall, a former military weatherman who says he spent three years with tall alien beings in that desert, tells it on the show and in his book Millennial Hospitality, citing park rangers. He takes it as a sign that the land was being guarded for some other reason.
